verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents a first-party MTTX analytics page that visualizes metrics and groups them by team, service, severity and other fields. It also documents an Alerting Analytics page showing how events become alerts, how many alerts are acknowledged, and how many become incidents. That covers the core MTTA/MTTR and incident-load parts of the story, but on-call health and explicit trend-over-time views are not evidenced. Missing for 10: on-call health metrics (burnout, pages per responder), explicit MTTA/MTTR trend-over-time documentation, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering leader, I get reliability analytics — MTTA/MTTR trends, incident load, on-call health — to see whether we are actually improving

citations.quote: This Analytics page groups and visualizes these metrics so you can understand overall health by entities like teams, impacted services, and more.
FireHydrant's analytics offer the ability to filter and group by various aspects
Use our new Alerting Analytics page to understand how incoming events are turning into Alerts, how many alerts are being acknowledged, and how many alerts are then turning into incidents.
